newsitem.title: POLAND: Peru rebels threaten to shoot hostages - Poland.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels threaten to shoot hostages - Poland.

text.p: Guerrillas holding hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima have threatened to start shooting the captives unless a doctor is sent to treat a wounded comrade, Poland's foreign minister said on Wednesday.

Dariusz Rosati told a news conference that Poland's charge d'affaires in Peru, Wojciech Tomaszewski, who was among at least 200 hostages being held by the leftist guerrillas, had phoned his wife from the residence and conveyed the demands.

"They are formulating very ultimatum-like demands for the doctor to come as fast as possible. Otherwise they say they will do what they have threatened from the beginning -- namely shooting hostages," Rosati said.
"One of the terrorists has been wounded, apparently in a shoot-out," he added.
Rosati said the rebels had also demanded the fastest possible start to negotiations with the Peruvian government but that these had apparently not yet started.
Rosati said he was optimistic for a favourable end to the crisis in which the guerrillas, after getting safety guarantees, would leave the embassy and free all the hostages.
"One can say this is fairly probable because they have achieved the propaganda effect of their action," he said.
"But there could also be considerably less optimistic scenarios, including the most tragic," he added.

He said Poland had called in the Peruvian ambassador and given him a note appealing to the government to do everything to ensure that nothing happened to the hostages and to resolve the crisis in a way that avoided bloodshed.
It had also called the Japanese ambassador and asked for full, running information on all measures taken by Tokyo.
The Polish ministry had set up a 10-strong crisis team in Warsaw and was ready to send diplomats to the spot if circumstances warranted, Rosati said.
